subject: Deal scale: sprint burn forecast & slotting for October closes
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ellen Cho <ellen@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deal scale: sprint burn forecast & slotting for October closes

Hi all — looping you in for this week's slotting + burn check for the Acme tranche. The close window is tightening and Acme has confirmed their expected traffic profile (see attached runrate). High-level asks: 

- Finance: confirm runway impact for the three reservation scenarios (base / expected / aggressive). I put draft numbers in Q4_runrate_sheet.xlsx (tab: scenarios).
- Infra: call out any hard constraints on dedicated pools and the earliest we can add 64/32/16-slot tranches without risking other commits.
- Sales: confirm the cadence of demo/po signatures that would trigger the next tranche. Marissa — want your read on conversion probability this week.

Agenda for Friday sync (30m):
1) Reconcile expected weekly-slot burn vs reserved capacity
2) Agree burst credits / fallback routing for first 6 weeks post-close
3) Action owners for procurement/contracting handoff

Ellen — thank you for the updated traffic profile. If procurement needs anything specific for the SOW, flag it here.

Attachments: Q4_runrate_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Cho <ellen@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal scale: sprint burn forecast & slotting for October closes

Jonas — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. Quick finance read: I populated three scenarios (base / expected / upside) with weekly burn and cash flow impact. Top-line from our side:

- Base: 40 reserved slots, expected weekly token burn ~1.2B tokens — incremental monthly cost +$85k.
- Expected: 64 reserved slots, weekly token burn ~1.9B tokens — incremental monthly cost +$150k.
- Aggressive: 96 reserved slots + burst, weekly token burn ~2.8B tokens — incremental monthly cost +$230k.

Open question: how many of those tokens can be covered by prefix caching on our side vs on Acme's side (that will materially change the compute hours). I left a note in the sheet (tab: caching_assumptions).

Action asks from finance:
- Ben / Infra: confirm the mapping from slots -> expected GPU-hours under the current runtime optimizations (quantization 4-bit path and KV caching assumptions). We need the mapping to finalize projected spend to OC split.
- Sales: if we cannot meet the "Expected" reservations by the targeted start-of-quarter date, finance needs a backup plan for incremental burst credits (and an estimate of how long credits will be needed).

I'll be on the Friday sync; if you want a pre-read, I can post the scenario summary to the Drive link Jonas included.

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance — Cloud Products
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Cho <ellen@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal scale: sprint burn forecast & slotting for October closes

Laura / Jonas — flagged a few infra constraints after running the slot->GPU-hour conversion against current pool utilization. Summary: 

- Realistic immediate commit we can guarantee by 2026-10-15: 48 slots mapped across nimbus-1 pool (mostly A100-equivalent). Any request above that number will require either rebalancing or the use of burst lanes.
- Earliest we can provision additional 48-slot tranche without disrupting current reserve SLAs: 2026-10-29 (hardware arrivals + validation).
- Fallbacks: we can provide 20% extra burst capacity for 6-week windows via preemptible pools but with higher P99 latency; recommend gating that to non-latency-sensitive endpoints.

Attached: gpu_pool_delta.csv (CSV) — includes slot->GPU-hour matrix under the three quantization/kv-cache assumptions Laura mentioned. Key asks for sales/finance:

- Confirm whether Acme will accept a staged start: 48 reserved slots at close + burst for first 4 weeks, with a hard provision on 2026-10-29 for the add-on 48. If Acme needs 96 effective slots day-one with low P99 SLO, we need an explicit premium for guaranteed burst and a formal SLA amendment.
- If finance wants to avoid burst credits, we can re-prioritize a small fraction of non-critical commitments for that week, but that has business impact (list available on request).

I'll also bring a short runbook to Friday's call showing routing policies (priority lanes, model-variant fallbacks) so Sales has a clear story to present.

Ben Carter
Infra Ops — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Cho <ellen@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal scale: sprint burn forecast & slotting for October closes

Thanks everyone — quick alignment from Sales side after reviewing the scenarios: 

- We can commit to the staged start Ben proposed: 48 slots day-one (close) + preemptible burst for weeks 1-4. The customer is comfortable with a staged approach if we formalize the SLA for latency-sensitive routes and offer a 10% credit for any missed P99 on those routes during the first 6 weeks.
- Conversion cadence: signatures expected by 2026-10-14 (legal is finalizing SOW). If that slips into the last week of October, we should expect them to ask for earlier burst guarantees.
- Action items: 
  - Jonas: update the Drive scenario to include the staged acceptance language and the SLA credit figure.
  - Laura: produce final cost forecast for staged + full provisioning so Sales can present tradeoffs on Friday.
  - Ben: publish the short runbook + confirm the provision date for the 2nd tranche (2026-10-29) in the runbook.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive — Sales
Redwood Inference
